amendments: A. Blocked operator pairs are now explicit applicability probes (DEFINED/UNDEFINED/INAPPLICABLE), asked before any transformation judgment.
B. W disambiguated from T at the ontology level: participant-in-act vs non-participating observer, each with its own explicit prose clause.
not_amended: No other v1 case was altered. v1 scores were not used to adjust any individual v2 answer.

ontology.third_party_added: A third person TAKES PART IN THE ACT, carrying it out together with the agent. The act itself is different because of them.
ontology.witness_bound_to_agent: A third person TAKES NO PART in the act; they observe it and are affiliated with the person who did the act, as it stands at the end.
ontology.witness_bound_to_recipient: A third person TAKES NO PART in the act; they observe it and are affiliated with the person who received the act, as it stands at the end.

applicability_semantics.DEFINED: The operation can be carried out and would change the description.
applicability_semantics.UNDEFINED: Blocked by ABSENCE — what the operation needs is not in the description.
applicability_semantics.INAPPLICABLE: Blocked by PRESENCE — what the operation would introduce is already there.

change_probe:
Which of the following changed between the first and the second? Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

Allowed values: roles_reversed, response_flipped, act_flipped, third_party_added, response_removed, witness_bound_to_agent, witness_bound_to_recipient, witness_rebound

If nothing changed, return an empty list.

Format: {"changed": ["...", "..."]}

applicability.operation_description: Swap the two people: whoever did the act now receives it, and whoever responded is now responded to.

Now consider this operation:
